v01.h2: YOU JUST DON'T WANT TO SEE IT
v01.txt: She's cheating on you. You just don't want to see it. You saw the phone flip over when you walked in. You saw her answer at midnight and laugh at nothing. And you told yourself you were imagining things. You're not. People who hide something always leave traces, and those traces are still there — the chats she deleted, the contact saved under a fake name, the messages that come in when you're asleep. You don't need her phone and you don't need to fight about it again. Type her number, read it yourself, and stop being the last one to know.

v02.txt: Everyone already knows. You're the last one. Her friends know, they've covered for her, and they laugh about it when you're not in the room. You feel stupid asking questions and getting the same answer every time: you're crazy, you're insecure, you're imagining it. You're not imagining anything. Whoever hides something leaves a trail behind, and the trail is still on that phone — deleted chats, hidden contacts, messages at two in the morning. Type her number and read it with your own eyes. Then decide what you do.

v03.txt: She calls you crazy, paranoid, insecure. She does it because it works. Every time you ask, you end up apologizing, and she ends up free to do it again. Notice what happens: the phone goes face down, notifications go silent, she takes it to the bathroom. That's not privacy, that's a pattern. And people who hide something always leave traces behind. You don't have to guess, argue or touch her phone. Type her number, see the conversations she deleted, and find out who you really live with.

v04.txt: She sleeps holding her phone. Ask yourself why. Nobody protects a screen like that when there's nothing on it. You know the routine: it lights up at midnight, she turns it face down, she says it's her mother. Then she deletes the thread, just in case. Here's what she doesn't know — deleted doesn't mean gone. The chats, the contacts saved with fake names, the photos she sent when you were asleep, all of it leaves a trail. Type her number and read it yourself, tonight, before she changes it.

v05.txt: You pay the bills. Somebody else is paying for her attention. That's the part nobody says out loud. You work, you come home, you get an excuse and a phone turned face down. And you still ask yourself if you're the problem. You're not. Whoever hides something leaves traces behind: deleted conversations, contacts with fake names, messages that arrive at two in the morning. Stop asking her, stop fighting, stop waiting for the truth to show up on its own. Type her number and read everything yourself.

v06.txt: Two years of lies and you're still the one apologizing. Think about how many times you brought it up and walked away feeling guilty. That's not love, that's control. And it only works while you have no proof. Listen: everything she deleted is still recoverable. The chats, the hidden contacts, the messages she answers with the screen tilted away from you. It takes sixty seconds and you never touch her phone. Type her number, look at the truth, and stop apologizing for being right.

v07.txt: She changed the password and got angry when you noticed. That's your answer right there. Honest people don't lock the door and then blame you for knocking. You already know the signs: the phone face down, the sudden silent mode, the shower with the phone inside. What she doesn't know is that the conversations she deletes stay in the backup, and the backup can be read. No app on her phone, no fight, no begging. Type her number and see exactly who has been texting her at night.

v08.txt: He's already inside your house. He sleeps in your bedroom every night, through her phone. She answers him while you watch TV next to her, then she laughs and says it's work. You feel it, you say something, and she turns it around on you. Here's the part she never thought about: deleted messages are not gone, and hidden contacts are still contacts. You don't touch her phone and you don't ask her anything. Type the number, read the last conversations, and find out how long it's been going on.

v09.txt: You apologize and she keeps lying. That's the deal you've been living with. Every doubt becomes a fight, every fight becomes your fault, and nothing ever changes. Stop trying to win an argument you can't prove. Whoever hides something leaves traces behind, and they're all still there: chats she erased, contacts under a fake name, messages that come in at two in the morning. Sixty seconds, her number, and you read it on your own phone. Then the conversation is over, because you'll already know.

v10.txt: She says it's just a friend. Friends don't text at two in the morning, and friends don't get saved under a fake name. You've seen the screen light up and go dark before you could read it. You've heard the excuse so many times you started believing it. Don't. Every deleted chat, every hidden contact, every photo she sent while you were asleep leaves a trail behind. Type her number, open the conversations yourself, and see what kind of friend that really is.
